## New investigation ideas

- **[2026-10-25] The live portfolio has a mechanical Exit on Edenred after its 9.5% fall on 10-21, and it still lists the cause as "unconfirmed". The cause is public: the Q3 revenue release that day. It hits the one claim the thesis rests on.** [[finance/trading-portfolio]] shows EDEN as 🔴 Exit since 10-22 (RSI 38, below SMA50, full exit recommended, not executed). Q3 total revenue was €725m, flat as reported and −1.3% like-for-like. Press reports blame the Italy and Brazil merchant-fee caps; organic growth excluding them was +6.6%, Mobility grew double digits, and FY guidance was kept (EBITDA −10% to −7% LFL). [[finance/ideas/idea-eden-red]] argues the caps are "already priced in" ("the horse has bolted"). A revenue decline from those same caps, still showing up a year later, is the test of that claim. **Next step:** read the 10-21 release (edenred.com press releases) and answer two of the page's unticked Key Questions: post-cap take rates in Brazil and Italy, and when the cap effect laps. Then decide whether the exit is a thesis break or a chart reflex, which is the 10-07 and 10-10 question now with data. This run found the release only through a web search; nothing in the wiki has ingested it.

- **[2026-10-25] Cooking is the only recommender domain that never learns what Fred actually did with a recommendation. After 17 weekly runs and 51 suggestions, the recipe recommender's only "memory" is a five-row recipes.md frozen since June.** Books marks reading status (✅/🆕 on [[books/reading-list]], reused by [[books/books-from-podcasts]]). Podcasts tags listened episodes `completed` (for example [[podcasts/podcast-odd-lots-french-political-crisis]]), and the summarizer and this task both work from what Fred heard. Cooking has nothing like this. The recommender's Step 1 treats [[cooking/recipes]] as the list of dishes to avoid repeating, but nothing ever adds a cooked suggestion to it. [[cooking/cooking-overview]]'s "Define focus" todo and empty "Techniques to Master" list are unchanged since 2026-05-01, so the recommender's Fred profile is still its own hard-coded guess. **Next step:** add a one-word status marker to each suggestion in [[cooking/recipe-suggestions]] (cooked / liked / skip), or a short cooked-log. Then change recipe-recommender Step 1 to weight chefs and cuisines by what got cooked. That is the same outcome-scoring Finance's strategy-feedback loop already applies to trade ideas. The 10-09 Health-targets idea needs this too: it can't tell whether more oily fish is getting cooked without a record of what is cooked.

## New cross-domain connections

- **[2026-10-25] Fred's Edenred thesis says France is the one market where regulation risk is "not over". The Odd Lots episode Fred just listened to describes a French fiscal crunch that bears on that risk.** [[finance/ideas/idea-eden-red]] lists "What is the French regulatory timeline and likely outcome?" as an unticked Key Question and notes that the product began as a *tax-advantaged* food allowance. [[podcasts/podcast-odd-lots-french-political-crisis]] argues France needs credible fiscal consolidation that its politics can't pass, with gridlock likely through 2027. That cuts both ways for EDEN. A tax exemption is exactly the kind of tax expenditure a desperate budget trims, which threatens volume, not just take rate. But gridlock also makes it less likely that the pending commission-cap reform gets passed, which supports the "priced in" case. Edenred is the only French-domiciled company among Fred's six EUR holdings in [[finance/trading-portfolio]], so the Odd Lots tail-risk framework applies to it most directly, and nothing currently links the two pages. Worth checking alongside the 10-25 Q3 idea before acting on the exit.

## New Investigation Ideas

- **[2026-10-24] Fred's whole automation stack is 30 scheduled-task prompts, and none of them is under version control. Today's newly listened podcast says that is the first thing to fix, because a model upgrade can quietly make a skill worse.** [[podcasts/podcast-growth-podcast-effective-loops-in-claude]] (Tyler Folkman on *The Growth Podcast*) gives two rules for Claude Code loops: make the validation gate deterministic, and keep skills in version control so you can roll back when a model change degrades them. `C:\Users\Mike\.claude\scheduled-tasks\` holds 30 task folders and has no `.git`. Two things the wiki already records make this more than theory. First, memory/index.md Key Decisions says `update_scheduled_task` *overwrites* SKILL.md, and that portfolio-management-briefing keeps its full instructions in SKILL.md with a "never call update" rule as the only protection. Second, the 2026-10-10 root cause of the fabricated trade was wording inside a briefing task's instructions (autonomous Turso-write steps), found only by reconstruction because there was no diff history to look at. The market-watchlist pipeline and fred-dashboard are already in private GitHub repos, so the habit exists; it just stops at the prompts. This differs from the 2026-10-13 pre-flight-check idea, which is about the *gate* on data; this is about the *instructions* themselves. **Next step:** `git init` the scheduled-tasks folder (private remote, or local only), commit the current state as a baseline, and add a one-line note to memory/index.md Key Decisions. Then, when a task's output changes character, `git log -p` on its SKILL.md/instructions.md shows whether the prompt changed or the model did. Check first that no task folder holds secrets (.env, tokens) before pushing anywhere.

## New Cross-Domain Connections

- **[2026-10-24] The guest Fred just listened to has spent ten years arguing that the half of the Magic Formula Fred's Strategy A relies on, the ROIC "quality" leg, is the half that loses money. Strategy A is now 1 for 12.** [[podcasts/podcast-behind-the-balance-sheet-tobias-carlisle]] is Tobias Carlisle's case that value is due a comeback. His acquirer's multiple (EV ÷ operating earnings) is Greenblatt's earnings yield turned upside down, with the return-on-capital ranking removed. In his published work (*Deep Value*, 2014) he reports that ranking on cheapness alone beat the full Magic Formula in backtests. His reason is mean reversion: a very high ROIC usually means peak margins, so the formula's "good *and* cheap" intersection keeps picking cyclicals at their earnings peak. [[books/book-little-book-beats-market]] presents that same intersection as the formula's whole edge. Fred's own results match Carlisle's warning more than Greenblatt's promise. [[finance/models/model-portfolio-management]] shows Strategy A at 1/12. Its 10-04 review found half the new Magic Formula passes were precious-metals miners, and the 10-11 review proposed a Materials-sector guard on the candidate query. The 10-19 idea above flagged CF Industries (P/E 8.6, ROIC 24.5%) as a likely peak-earnings cyclical. The sector guard is a patch on the symptom, while Carlisle names the cause, and the two give a testable choice. Re-rank the last ~12 Strategy A entries by EV/EBIT alone and see whether the cyclicals drop out or rise. If they rise, the guard is the right fix. If they fall away, ROIC is the leg doing the damage. The capital-cap exits still confound realised returns, so use the 10-04 forward-return method, not closed P&L.

2 new: *Soldier of Fortune* (Tobias Carlisle), *The Art of War* (Sun Tzu), both from Behind the Balance Sheet #64.
